npm_test.judgement_of_the_reasoning: SOUND, and this gate agrees the green run is the point rather than a weakness. The argument is: request<T> (web/src/api/client.ts:158-169) ends in `return response.json() as Promise<T>` and T is erased at runtime, so client.get<User[]> and client.get<GroupMemberPage> are byte-identical against the same spy body. This gate verified that premise directly -- the pre-fix source at d28c3cf6:web/src/api/identity.ts:58-59 is `members: (id) => client.get<User[]>(...)`, verbatim pass-through with no unwrap, so no runtime assertion could ever discriminate it. The pairing of (tsc exit 2, five diagnostics) with (runtime suite green) is exactly the demonstration required: it shows the detector that decision (b) chose is real AND that the detector the suite would otherwise rely on is blind. A mutant that broke both would have proved far less, because it would not have isolated the type-only channel.

caveat_N1_verdict.finding: CONFIRMED GENUINE. There is no diagnostic for the design's `:228` reasoning (`user.user_id` not existing on GroupMember). In the mutant's own numbering that site is line 229 (`const id = user.id ?? user.user_id ?? ''`), and tsc emits nothing there.
caveat_N1_verdict.why_the_absence_is_correct_and_not_a_def: The `.map` on line 228 fails to resolve on `GroupMemberPage | never[]`, so its callback parameter `user` is never contextually typed and falls to implicit any -- reported as TS7006 at (228,41). A property access on `any` is not an error, so line 229 cannot produce a diagnostic. The design's prediction was contingent on the `.map` resolving, which it does not. This is the exact characteristic the Step 2b gate predicted when it flagged the predicted list as a FLOOR.
caveat_N1_verdict.no_manufacture: The mutant was NOT adjusted to produce a :228 diagnostic, and this gate would have FAILED the step had it been. Four distinct source positions and five diagnostics are well above the floor.

M-1b.discrimination_verdict: The two directions together do discriminate this specific trap rather than merely breaking something. M-1a breaks only at the consumer sites when the producer's type is kept; M-1b breaks only at the producer/consumer boundary when the producer's type is reverted; in neither direction does the runtime suite move. That is a matched pair, not one mutation that happens to break a build.

judgement_on_the_unplanned_M1b_observati.verdict: AGREE with the characterisation, and it is the correct call rather than a cautious one.
judgement_on_the_unplanned_M1b_observati.verification_performed: The claim is factually correct and this gate confirmed it two ways. (1) Statically: lines 212, 213 and 214 of the committed web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts are exactly `expect(result.items.length).toBe(1)`, `expect(result.count).toBe(1)` and `expect(result.next_cursor).toBeNull()`, and column 19 is the first character after `result.` on each. judgement_on_the_unplanned_M1b_observati.why_the_classification_is_right: Fail-first evidence must come from the UNMODIFIED test run against the UNMODIFIED pre-fix code. This signal exists only because the shipped type was mutated, which puts it in the same category as M-1a's own diagnostics -- a mutation-derived detector, not a pre-fix red. Promoting it to fail-first evidence would also be wrong on a second ground: it detects drift in the DECLARED return type, not drift in the actual runtime shape, so a backend that changed its envelope while the TypeScript declaration stayed put would sail past it. Calling it 'an additional compile-time detector' is exactly as strong a claim as the evidence supports.
judgement_on_the_unplanned_M1b_observati.one_qualification: It is slightly overstated to call the detector unanticipated in kind. Design section 7.1 already nominated tsc as the detector for decision (b) ('tsc -b tsconfig.json ... catches every one on every run'). What is genuinely new is that the TEST FILE participates in that detection surface, which neither the design nor the Step 2b gate said. Minor wording point; it does not change the verdict and needs no rework.
